transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Alex (CedarBridge Head of Search), Dana (Platform), Tom (Data Scientist), Lena (Security)

[00:00] Jamie (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jamie, account lead for this region at Redwood. Priya and Marcus from our solutions team are here to dig into the embedding/rerank needs. Alex, do you want to kick off with context?

[00:18] Alex (Head of Search): Yeah hi, thanks. so CedarBridge is building conversational help + transaction search inside our customer portal. Primary ask: we need high precision ranked results for financial docs and statements, lots of short queries, sometimes multi-turn. We're evaluating embeddings + rerank, need to decide hosted vs dedicated vs private. Security is heavy for us — PCI-adjacent. Also latency matters — sub-200ms tail ideally for rerank path.

[00:38] Priya (SE): Great, that's helpful. can you share current architecture? are you using a vector DB today?

[00:45] Dana (Platform): We currently use a sharded Faiss setup on VMs for embeddings (in-house). It's a pain to manage at scale. We compute 512-d embeddings with an internal model, store with metadata. Rerank is a separate transformer scorer running per top-50 results. Throughput currently peaks around 300 qps, and ops costs are ballooning. We're trying to see if Redwood's hosted API can reduce ops, or if Dedicated gives better tail latency and cost predictability.

[01:10] Marcus (SE): Ok. worth discussing hybrid search patterns — we commonly see a fanout retrieve to your vector store for top-N then a fast reranker on Redwood to re-score top-k. That gives a good balance between latency and quality. You mentioned 512 dims — what's the target recall/K?

[01:29] Tom (Data Scientist): We typically fetch top-200, then rerank top-20 for UI. But top-50 rerank was more stable in earlier tests, we might tighten to top-20 for latency. Another variable is embedding dimension — our research shows 512 is decent for financial short texts, but 768 or 1,024 improves semantic nuance. Concern is throughput and storage cost.

[01:51] Alex: Also interested in hybrid routing — sometimes prefer lexical BM25 for transaction IDs, but embeddings for fuzzy matches. So we want a system that smartly routes queries based on heuristics or model confidence.

[02:06] Priya: Redwood supports hybrid routing policy — at the request layer you can route by query classifier or by rule (e.g., regex for txn IDs). We can also do a combined score: lexical score + rerank model score. For Dedicated/Private, that routing runs locally with no cross-cloud hops. For Hosted, routing lives in Redwood control plane but we can pin rerank traffic to dedicated capacity.

[02:30] Lena (Security): quick question — on Hosted, data residency and KMS, we'll need to know how tokens are stored, logs retention, and whether customer-managed KMS is supported.

[02:40] Jamie: Yes, hosted supports customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest, but private deployments give you full KMS/HSM in your VPC. We'll send the SOC2 and more detailed security pack after this call.

[02:53] Alex: What's the timeline for Dedicated vs Private onboarding? If we choose Dedicated reserved capacity, how quickly can we go live?

[03:01] Marcus: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 2-4 weeks from contract if we already have the model choices. Private (VPC) is 6-8 weeks — includes networking and KMS setup. Hosted can be immediate for early testing.

[03:12] Tom: For rerank model — are you hosting open models or do you recommend Redwood models? We need explainability.

[03:20] Priya: We support curated open models (e.g., Llama family variants, Mistral) and Redwood-verified performance profiles. For rerank we often recommend mid-sized models (7B-13B) with quantization for latency, or a distilled reranker to stay in sub-200ms tail. We can also run custom models you bring in Dedicated/Private.

[03:41] Alex: Okay, about vector DB integration — can Redwood call out to our Faiss clusters, or do we need to migrate to a managed store?

[03:49] Marcus: Two approaches: 1) keep Faiss and call it as your primary retriever, use Redwood for embedding generation and rerank; 2) migrate vectors to our managed store and let Redwood handle retrieval + rerank. Option 1 reduces migration effort; option 2 gives you batching, caching, and smart sharding handled by Redwood and often lowers tail latency.

[04:12] Dana: If we keep our Faiss, what about network hops and extra serialization? Concerned about cross-VPC egress and latency.

[04:19] Priya: We can colocate Dedicated capacity in your VPC (Private) so Redis/Faiss calls are local. For Hosted, you can run a private connector via secure tunnel but that adds ms. We recommended Dedicated if tail latency and egress costs are a big concern.

[04:36] Alex: Perf numbers — can you give us an example: rerank of top-20 using a 13B model quantized to 4-bit on Dedicated, what's the per-request latency range?

[04:47] Marcus: On Dedicated with optimized kernels and batch size 1, 13B quant 4-bit reranker typically 60–150ms p50–p95 for single-token scoring runs, but end-to-end (retrieve + rerank + merge) often ends up around 120–220ms depending on your retrieval latency. If you use a distilled 3B reranker, p95 can go under 100ms.

[05:09] Tom: We have many short queries with small contexts, does Redwood support prefix KV caching or caching of rerank results?

[05:17] Priya: Yes — Redwood Optimize supports prefix/KV caching and result-level caching for exact-match queries. We can cache rerank outputs for repeated queries and share TTLs across routes. That reduces tokens consumed and latency for heavy repeated queries.

[05:31] Alex: About embedding dims — what's the cost tradeoff? 512 vs 1536 storage and query cost difference?

[05:39] Marcus: Roughly linear: 3x dims ~ 3x storage and larger index size — which affects retrieval times and RAM. For throughput, higher dims increase compute on similarity search and memory bandwidth. We often recommend using 512–768 for most short financial queries and 1,024+ only when you need fine-grained semantic nuance. We'll provide a cost model for your data volume.

[05:59] Dana: On Faiss shard counts — we've been rebalancing; what's Redwood's guidance for sharding when ingesting 100M vectors?

[06:06] Priya: For 100M vectors, typical shard sizes target fit-in-memory per node (e.g., 8–32GB per shard). If using IVF+PQ, you can compress and reduce memory, but that increases recall/latency tradeoffs. Redwood's managed store can autoscale shards and handle rebalancing for you.

[06:24] Alex: Security — if we bring our own model weights for rerank, will Redwood ever persist weights outside our environment?

[06:31] Jamie: No, if you opt for Private deployment your weights remain in your environment. For Dedicated, we can set tenancy and contractual protections; for Hosted you can bring models but they'd run in Redwood infra unless Private. We'll capture this in the security pack.

[06:45] Tom: How do you support hybrid ranking: combining BM25 + embedding similarity + ML reranker score? We need to normalize scores for UI.

[06:53] Marcus: Redwood can return the component scores and a combined normalized score. You can tune weights per route. We also provide tooling to sweep weight combinations against held-out labels and produce precision@k curves.

[07:10] Alex: There are also procurement questions — in enterprise, do you do annual reserved capacity discounts and usage caps?

[07:18] Jamie: Yes, Dedicated includes commit pricing and guarantees; we can structure tiered pricing. Hosted is usage-based. We'll share pricing ranges for your 1k qps baseline in the follow-up.

[07:29] Lena: Quick compliance Q — log retention and redaction: our legal requires redaction of PIIs and retention windows per EU region. Does Redwood redact automatically?

[07:38] Priya: We offer configurable redaction rules and per-tenant retention policies. In Private deployment you can control retention entirely. We'll include details in the security docs.

[07:48] Alex: Ok, let's dig into a sample flow. Tom, can you walk through an example query?

[07:55] Tom (Data Scientist): Sure. Query: "why was my direct deposit delayed May 2" — we'd like BM25 to catch exact term "direct deposit" and dates, embeddings to get context, then rerank candidate statements and one-paragraph docs. We want to boost documents with status metadata. Also need to surface the source doc and confidence.

[08:18] Priya: For that flow we'd recommend creating a small pre-classifier route: if query contains date tokens or regex for txn ids, route to lexical-first retrieval; if not, embedding-first. Then retrieve top-200, filter by metadata (status), and rerank top-20 with a lightweight 3B scorer. That will likely keep p95 under 200ms.

[08:37] Dana: For metadata filters, can Redwood push filters down to the vector store? We want to avoid post-filtering big sets.

[08:43] Marcus: Yes, if metadata is indexed alongside vectors in the same store we push filters into the retriever call. For external Faiss we support metadata filtering via an indexable sidecar or ANN that supports attributes. For managed store, it's native.

[08:58] Alex: Demo request — can we see a short demo of rerank quality and latency?

[09:03] Jamie: Absolutely — we can run a demo but given time constraints maybe better to schedule a dedicated smoke test with your sample queries. We'll demo once we have your sample set.

[09:12] Tom: We'll share a 500-query sample and relevancy labels. Expect some noise.

[09:18] Priya: Perfect. On the topic of benchmarking: we recommend running both a hosted pilot to validate relevance and a Dedicated smoke test for tail latency and cost. For the Dedicated run we'll provision GPUs and run 1k qps fanout simulation to measure tail.

[09:33] Alex: 1k qps is our internal target for peak traffic. Is Redwood able to simulate mixed workload: retrieval-heavy vs rerank-heavy?

[09:41] Marcus: Yes, our perf harness supports mixed workloads and will report p50/p95/p99 across pipeline stages. We'll provide a runbook.

[09:49] Dana: What about batching strategies — you mentioned continuous batching earlier. If we get bursts, how will Redwood balance batch size to meet latency SLAs?

[09:58] Priya: There's a tradeoff: larger batches raise throughput efficiency but increase tail latency. Redwood allows policy-based batching with SLO caps; Dedicated nodes can be tuned to favor latency with smaller max batch sizes, and we have preemption policies for high-priority requests.

[10:14] Alex: Pricing question: is reranking priced per token or per request?

[10:18] Jamie: For hosted, model inference is per-token + per-request overhead. For Dedicated we offer instance-hour pricing plus a small per-token accounting for telemetry. We'll include concrete numbers in the follow-up.

[10:28] Tom: We're also considering quantized embeddings at ingest to save storage. Any downsides for retrieval quality?

[10:34] Marcus: PQ and quantization can reduce recall slightly; PQ on embeddings is common for 100M+ scale. If you have strict relevance SLAs, we recommend hybrid: hot index (uncompressed) for recent/most-critical docs and cold compressed shards. Redwood's managed index supports that.

[10:51] Alex: Any gotchas with bringing our own Faiss index to Redwood rerank?

[10:56] Priya: Two practical items: 1) alignment of similarity metric (cosine vs inner product) must match your embedding model and index; 2) metadata filter support requires a compatible sidecar or index format. We'll help with a compatibility checklist.

[11:12] Lena: If we choose Dedicated, who handles patching and kernel updates for GPUs?

[11:17] Marcus: Redwood-managed Dedicated includes runtime and kernel updates; for Private on-prem we provide the ops package and runbook, but you control patch cadence.

[11:26] Alex: Let's talk success criteria for a POC: what should we validate?

[11:31] Priya: Typical POC criteria: relevance improvement over baseline (e.g., +X% NDCG or precision@10), p95 latency target met for 95% of traffic, cost per 1k queries within your budget, integration simplicity (connector tests), and security/compliance gating.

[11:48] Tom: For relevance we'll measure precision@20 and business impact metric for support deflection. We'll share labels.

[11:55] Jamie: Great. wrapping up — recap and next steps. We'll send SOC2 + security pack, an initial pricing estimate for Hosted and Dedicated at 1k qps, and a smoke-test runbook. CedarBridge will send sample queries and labels. We'll schedule the Dedicated smoke test for next Thursday if that works?

[12:12] Alex: Next Thursday works for our infra team. Dana will coordinate availability.

[12:18] Dana: noted. I'll send calendar invite once we confirm slots.

[12:21] Jamie: thanks everyone. we'll follow up after call with documents and action items.

[12:27] (call ends)
